source.name: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters
source.citation: Planck Collaboration, Aghanim N. et al. 2020, A&A 641, A6 (2018 results; 2020A&A...641A...6P)
source.licence: Values quoted from the published paper; numerical facts, freely citable with attribution.

OmegaK.description: Curvature — assumed exactly flat, as the base LCDM model does.

OmegaR.description: Radiation (photons + 3 massless neutrinos), Omega_r h^2 = 4.15e-5. Negligible below z ~ 100 but included in the integrals.

lastScattering.description: Recombination / the surface of last scattering — the CMB. The limit of what can be seen.
lastScattering.publishedPlanckNote: Planck 2018 VI quotes the comoving angular-diameter distance D_M(z*) = 13869.6 Mpc for the base model. Our value is computed here from the frozen parameters above and agrees to better than 1%; prefer our computed value so the number and the transform cannot drift apart.
lastScattering.uiLabel: the limit of what can be seen — 13.787 billion years of light travel. NOT "the edge of the universe".

particleHorizon.description: Comoving distance light could have travelled since t=0 (z -> infinity): the radius of the observable universe. This — not the CMB shell — is the ~14,300 Mpc / 46.5 Gly figure usually quoted. The CMB shell sits just inside it.

distanceRecipes.note: Which transform to use at which scale. Never mix them silently.
rules: Where a distance modulus exists (UNGC, Cosmicflows-4), use it directly: d_L = 10**(DM/5 - 5) Mpc. No cosmology is assumed and no H0 enters.
Below z ~ 0.1 (2MRS, essentially all of it), d ~ cz / H0 is accurate to better than ~5%.
Beyond that, integrate D_C = (c/H0) * int_0^z dz'/E(z'), E(z) = sqrt(Om(1+z)^3 + Or(1+z)^4 + OL).
Luminosity distance d_L = (1+z) D_C; angular-diameter distance d_A = D_C / (1+z). For a flat universe these differ from D_C by factors that matter past z ~ 0.1.

h0Tension.description: The early-universe (CMB) and late-universe (distance-ladder) measurements of H0 disagree at about 5 sigma. This is an open problem in cosmology, not a rounding error, and the UI surfaces it rather than hiding it.

sh0es.method: Cepheid-calibrated SNe Ia distance ladder, late universe

cosmicflows4Internal.warning: CF4 distances are calibrated to H0 = 74.6 while this module uses 67.4. Mixing a CF4 distance with a cz/H0 distance puts a ~10% radial seam exactly at the scale transition. Use the CF4 distance modulus directly wherever CF4 is being rendered and disclose the scale.

h0Tension.uiNote: How fast the universe expands is measured two ways that do not agree: 67.4 km/s/Mpc from the cosmic microwave background, 73.0 from nearby supernovae. OmniAtlas renders with the Planck value; distances beyond the Local Group carry this ~8% systematic.
